items.title: dell-5530 maintenance window: rotate leaked node token, re-parent orphaned Scheduled Task, decide auto-logon
items.description: One window closes three things at once. The node token was exposed in a transcript on 2026-09-09 and is still live (risk bounded to LAN: agent binds 192.168.1.250:8790, node not on tailnet). The agent is ALSO orphaned from its Scheduled Task (task state Ready, LastTaskResult 0x8007042B) so Stop-ScheduledTask is a no-op and RestartOnFailure gives no auto-restart. Costs all 6 ConPTY sessions - they are in-process children of the agent and cannot survive a restart by design. Runbook is in the multi-node memory note.
acceptance_criteria: Snapshot sessions + each running claude's transcript id before shutdown
Graceful POST /v1/internal/shutdown (schtasks /end is a no-op on the orphan)
New token written to C:\Users\tranv\.terminal-mcp\node-agent.token AND controller node-agent-tokens.env
Start-ScheduledTask; task state shows Running and tracks the live agent
Old token returns 401, new token 200, verified from the node side
Decide BootTrigger vs LogonType=InteractiveToken (auto-logon) - do NOT switch to S4U without checking the show_on_desktop ConPTY path
Sessions recreated and claude --resume'd per snapshot

items.title: Rate-limit / lockout on node-agent bearer auth
items.description: Token comparison is constant-time but unbounded: an attacker on the LAN (or on any network a node is exposed to) can attempt tokens indefinitely. Found in the 2026-09-09 internet-connectivity audit.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated 401s from one source are throttled or locked out
Legitimate heartbeat traffic (20s interval) is never throttled
Lockout state cannot wedge a node permanently

items.title: Node token rotation and revocation mechanism
items.description: There is no rotation/revocation path today - rotating a token is a manual, per-node, restart-requiring edit of two files (proven twice on 2026-09-09: macbook rotated, dell-5530 deferred because its restart costs 6 sessions). Roadmap Phase 5 names this.
acceptance_criteria: A token can be rotated without hand-editing files on both sides
Revocation takes effect without a full node restart, or the restart cost is documented per platform
Old token is provably rejected afterwards

items.title: Validate node endpoint scheme: refuse plaintext http:// to a non-private host
items.description: config.py accepts any non-empty string as nodes.remote[].endpoint. A plaintext http:// endpoint pointed at a public host would send the bearer token in the clear on every request. RemoteNodeClient already verifies TLS correctly for https:// - only the scheme check is missing.
acceptance_criteria: http:// to a public address is refused at config load with a clear error
http:// to a private/LAN/overlay address still works (today's deployments)
https:// unaffected

items.title: terminal-mcp-doctor reports 'lan: not configured' while the service IS LAN-bound
items.description: The CLI reads its OWN environment, not the running service's, so describe_endpoints reports loopback-only even though the service is bound to 192.168.1.132 and 100.81.85.120. The dashboard route is correct because it runs in-process. describe_endpoints' docstring claims it 'always reflects what the RUNNING process actually resolved' - true for the dashboard, false for the CLI.
acceptance_criteria: doctor reports the bind addresses the live service actually has
Or the docstring/output is corrected to say it reflects the CLI's own env
No false 'not configured' when a LAN/overlay bind is active

items.title: Live remote-node auto-dispatch smoke test through the real RemoteNodeClient
items.description: REQUIREMENTS Backlog item 1. Gate before config.queue.enabled can be turned on against any real lane. Needs 0 dropped / 0 duplicate dispatch across restart and reconnect. m910 is the low-risk candidate (tmux-backed, restart-safe since the KillMode fix); dell-5530 is not, its sessions cannot survive an agent restart.
acceptance_criteria: Auto-dispatch verified end-to-end against a real remote node
0 dropped and 0 duplicate dispatch across a controller restart
Same across a node reconnect

items.title: Direct-send reliability fix: deploy and live-reverify on dell-5530
items.description: REQUIREMENTS Backlog item 7. Fix is shipped locally; verifying it is Windows-ConPTY-specific and needs a real dell-5530 restart, so it rides the same maintenance window as the token rotation.
acceptance_criteria: Fix running on dell-5530
Direct send verified live on a real Windows session

items.title: Internet node transport: outbound WSS node->controller (roadmap Phase 2)
items.description: The 2026-09-09 audit's core finding: the data plane is controller->node (inbound to the node), so a NAT'd node is visible-but-uncontrollable - heartbeat lands, dashboard shows ONLINE, every real operation fails. Overlay VPN (now unblocked) is a workaround, not a fix; outbound WSS removes the inbound requirement entirely and is the only option that scales past hand-configured peers.
acceptance_criteria: A node behind NAT with no inbound port is fully controllable
Reconnect/backoff across sleep, Wi-Fi change and IP change without manual re-registration
Tasks enqueued while offline auto-dispatch on reconnect with no duplicates

items.title: Node self-registration with an enrollment token
items.description: An unknown node_id heartbeat is refused NODE_NOT_FOUND, and dashboard onboarding health-probes the node, so onboarding needs controller->node reachability AND a manual controller-side action. The goal 'install agent, paste token, it appears' is not achievable today.
acceptance_criteria: A new machine can enroll with only an enrollment token
No inbound reachability to the node required at enrollment
Enrollment is auditable and the token is single-use or scoped

items.title: registry_list / registry_search are not fleet-aware
items.description: REQUIREMENTS Backlog item 13. terminal_registry_reopen is fleet-aware and node_agent now exposes /v1/registry, but the list/search surfaces (MCP + dashboard Persistent Registry panel) remain local-node-only.
acceptance_criteria: registry_list/search span every online node
Dashboard Persistent Registry panel shows remote sessions
Per-node failure is tolerated like the other fleet reads

items.title: Codex --resume support for registry_reopen
items.description: REQUIREMENTS Backlog item 11. Claude has --resume wiring; Codex does not, so a recovered Codex session starts fresh. Relevant now that macbook and dell-5530 both run Codex.
acceptance_criteria: A recovered Codex session resumes its conversation
Resume is verified before success is reported (no fake resurrection)

items.title: macOS nodes report platform='linux' in the node registry
items.description: node_agent.py's heartbeat defaults platform='linux' and macOS uses that same path, so macbook is registered as linux. Cosmetic today but wrong for any platform-aware routing or capability decision later.
acceptance_criteria: A macOS node reports platform='macos' (or darwin) in the registry
Linux and Windows nodes unchanged
Dashboard/doctor show the real platform

items.title: Production session_registry is polluted with ~268 test-artifact rows
items.description: 268 of 513 rows are test session names (test-*, mcprec-*, lifecycle-*). Cause is known and documented in conftest: the live service observes test tmux sessions on the shared tmux server and records them. Harmless but noisy, and it makes the registry hard to read.
acceptance_criteria: Test-named rows cleaned out of the production registry
A documented periodic cleanup, or tests stop creating rows the live service picks up

items.title: Two pre-existing test_kill_reopen failures from stale tmux sessions
items.description: test_dashboard_kill_route_refuses_protected_session and test_dashboard_rename_route_refuses_protected_session fail on clean main too, with 'duplicate session: lifecycle-protected-dashboard-rename' - leftover sessions on the shared tmux server, not a code defect. They have been masking real signal in every full-suite run this session.
acceptance_criteria: Both pass on a clean checkout
The test cleans up or uniquifies its session name so it cannot collide again

items.title: Flaky tests under full-suite load
items.description: test_integration_loop::test_two_concurrent_loop_instances_never_double_merge_the_same_handoff, test_dashboard_nodes::test_nodes_list_shows_local_node_online_after_a_get and test_p0_hardening::test_prompt_injection_in_pane_output_remains_inert_data each failed once in a full run and passed in isolation on both the branch and clean main. Timing-sensitive; they cost real triage time repeatedly.
acceptance_criteria: Each is made deterministic or explicitly marked/quarantined
A full run is reproducibly green apart from known-skipped tests

items.title: Heartbeat replay protection (nonce/timestamp)
items.description: node_heartbeat authenticates the bearer token but has no nonce or timestamp, so a captured heartbeat can be replayed. Low impact today (LAN-only, and a heartbeat only writes metrics) but it is a real gap once nodes are on the internet.
acceptance_criteria: A replayed heartbeat is rejected
Clock skew tolerated sensibly

items.title: Audit rows are per-node, not centrally aggregated
items.description: Each node writes its own audit.db. There is no fleet-wide audit view, so answering 'who sent what, where' means reading N databases.
acceptance_criteria: Fleet-wide audit query across online nodes
Per-node failure tolerated like other fleet reads

items.title: Per-node config lineage requires a manual rebuild on every pull
items.description: m910's config derives from the Dell's config.yaml (rebuild on the new upstream base + re-apply 3 edits) while macbook's derives from config.example.yaml (preserve verbatim). Both are locally modified so every git pull refuses until config.yaml is checked out first. This is error-prone and was hand-done twice on 2026-09-09.
acceptance_criteria: Node-specific config is not a modified copy of a tracked file
A pull needs no manual config surgery
Existing per-node differences preserved

items.title: Review codex_yolo default (--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox)
items.description: SessionLifecycleConfig.codex_yolo defaults to True, so ANY deployment that never mentions the setting launches Codex with approvals and sandbox bypassed. Currently inert on m910/macbook (m910 has no codex; macbook now DOES, so it is live there). Decide whether the safe default should be False with an explicit opt-in.
acceptance_criteria: Default decided deliberately and documented
If it stays True, the risk is stated where an operator will see it
Per-node override is easy

items.title: P0.1 Give the runtime a project dimension (canonical project_id on lanes/tasks)
items.description: queue_lanes.project is NULL on all 35 lanes and queue_tasks has no canonical project. Backfill from each lane's session repo_root via project_identity/resolve_project_for_session. Columns already exist; additive.
acceptance_criteria: Lanes/tasks carry canonical project_id
'what is project X doing' answerable from the queue
Unresolvable lanes stay NULL, excluded from project views

notes: shipped, deployed, live-smoked

items.title: P0.2 Event bus (project-scoped, claimable, leased)
items.description: queue_events/integration_events/supervisor_events are three append-only per-store logs with no subscribe and no cross-store ordering. Build one events table with publish()/claim_next() reusing the BEGIN IMMEDIATE + lease pattern from claim_next_task.
acceptance_criteria: TASK_CREATED/TASK_READY/WORKER_DONE/VERIFY_PENDING/TEST_FAILED/USER_FEEDBACK published
A consumer cannot double-process an event
Existing per-store logs keep working and emit into the bus

notes: shipped, deployed, live-smoked

items.title: P0.3 Worker capability registry: tool/runtime axis (playwright, wpf, webview2, dotnet)
items.description: nodes has platform/session_backend/shell_capabilities/agent_types/wsl_available but nothing expresses tool capability, so Linux-HTML/Playwright vs Windows-WPF/WebView2 routing is impossible. labels exists and is empty everywhere. Detection must be probe-based like available_agent_types, never declared.
acceptance_criteria: Nodes report tool/runtime capabilities they actually have
Detection is probe-based, not configured
Routing can select a node by capability

notes: deployed; m910+macbook redeployed and reporting real capabilities

items.title: P0.4 Task lease API: claim/renew/release/handoff
items.description: queue_tasks.claim_token/lease_expires_at are stamped atomically already, but there is no renew/release/handoff verb for tasks (handoff exists only in the unused integration store). A worker crash should free a task deterministically.
acceptance_criteria: Task claim can be renewed and released explicitly
An expired lease is reclaimable and reconciles to the prior state
Handoff between workers preserves task identity and history

notes: deployed; renew/release/handoff live-smoked on the real queue store

items.title: P0.5 Verify queue with capability routing
items.description: Verification is currently a STATE of the same task in the same session (15 real VERIFIED), so a different worker cannot verify. Publish VERIFY_PENDING{project,capability} on WORKER_DONE and let a verifier claim by capability. Keep in-session verification as the default until a verifier pool exists.
acceptance_criteria: A verifier other than the worker can claim verification
Routing respects capability
Existing in-session verification still works unchanged

deploys: terminal-mcp-http.service on c5b43e5, dirty:false, 15/15 local sessions intact
notes: Verifier other than the worker CAN claim: proven live -- handoff local-verifier -> macbook-verifier, old token rejected NOT_LEASE_HOLDER.
Routing respects capability against the REAL fleet: [playwright,linux]->local, [windows]->dell-5530 (empty probed list, routed on reported platform), [windows,dotnet]->none.

In-session verification unchanged: opt-in is per task via completion_policy['verify']; no existing task carries it. Zero new task statuses, zero new transition edges (asserted structurally against VALID_TRANSITIONS).
Migration v7 verified on a copy of the real production queue.db: 38 tasks / 246 events, every row byte-identical, verify_jobs empty, re-apply a no-op.
macos deliberately NOT routable -- node agent has no Darwin branch, MacBook reports platform=linux. Documented, not papered over.

items.title: P0.6 Generalise pane lease into a named-resource ownership lock
items.description: lease.PaneLeaseStore is already pane_key-generic in everything but its name. Generalise to resource_key (file/module/branch) with the same TTL/owner/crash-recovery semantics.
acceptance_criteria: A named resource can be owned with a TTL
Expiry reclaims deterministically
Pane behaviour unchanged

deploys: terminal-mcp-http.service on da39470, dirty:false, 15/15 local sessions intact
notes: Generalised rather than duplicated: the pane lease's atomic check-and-set moved into _LeaseTable and now serves both subjects. PaneLeaseStore's generated SQL asserted BYTE-IDENTICAL to the shipped statement; its 14 existing tests pass untouched.
Separate resource_locks table in the same leases.db -- different lifetimes (20s vs minutes), and pane_leases is on core.py's send hot path.

Live-smoked on the real production leases.db: contention reports the holder, project scoping proven against a real second project, all-or-nothing multi-acquire, two real threads racing opposite orders with exactly one winner holding BOTH, operator override, and the pane lease still working afterwards. All rows cleaned up.
Migration v2 verified on a copy first: pane_leases byte-identical, resource_locks empty, re-apply a no-op.
ADVISORY, not enforcement -- and deliberately no waiter queue.

items.title: P0.7 Project-level MCP APIs for ChatGPT (status/submit_goal/events/report/pause/resume/assign)
items.description: 11 terminal_backlog_* tools plus terminal_project_list exist; project verbs do not. Pause/resume exist only per lane (LANE_PAUSED x6) and generalise.
acceptance_criteria: ChatGPT can ask project status and submit a goal
Project pause/resume works
Additive: all 134 existing tools unchanged

items.title: P1.1 Per-project event-driven coordinator via the existing scope_reasoner seam
items.description: CoordinatorGate is deterministic, fail-closed and production-used (32 decisions) but per-task/per-lane, and QueueLoop polls. Wrap it in a per-project consumer woken by bus events; the LLM is woken only to decompose/prioritise/resolve dependencies through the already-pluggable scope_reasoner. The deterministic dispatch gate must stay deterministic.
acceptance_criteria: Coordinator wakes on events, not polling
Coordinator state survives restart (store, not session context)
Dispatch safety stays fail-closed and deterministic

items.title: P1.2 Activate the integration/merge queue (built, 68 tests, 0 production rows)
items.description: integration_store/integration_engine already implement a project-scoped, leased, claimable handoff queue with conflict-rework routing and batches, fully tested, never used. Turning it on for one real project is the cheapest large win available.
acceptance_criteria: One real project runs a real handoff through merge
Conflict routes rework to the owning session, never auto-resolves content
Idempotent under restart

items.title: P2.1 Deterministic portfolio scheduler across projects
items.description: rebalance() only moves tasks between sessions inside one project label and depends on the unused planner. No cross-project allocation or priority arbitration exists. Needs P0.1 and P0.3 first.
acceptance_criteria: Resources allocated across projects by priority x capability x lease
No LLM in the scheduler
Dry-run preview before applying

items.title: P2.2 Preview-fast queue
items.description: No preview concept exists anywhere in source or DB. Needs its own runner plus PREVIEW_FAILED events.
acceptance_criteria: Preview runs automatically after a UI main update
PREVIEW_FAILED routes back as rework

items.title: Dashboard backlog panel: select by canonical project, not by local path
items.description: The panel could only be pointed at a local filesystem path, which names a CHECKOUT rather than a project and can only reach repos on the controller's own box. Adds a project picker over a new /dashboard/api/projects and threads project_id through all five backlog routes.
acceptance_criteria: Panel selects a project by canonical project_id
project_id reaches read AND every mutating route
A project with no local checkout is addressable

deploys: terminal-mcp-http.service on 9268ecf, dirty:false, 15/15 local sessions intact
notes: Found and fixed a REAL pre-existing bug: BACKLOG_HTML's inline <script> had literal newlines inside JS string literals (non-raw Python triple-quoted string), a syntax error that killed the WHOLE script -- the panel had never run any JavaScript. No existing test parsed the JS.
Regression guarded two ways (narrow pure-Python check + node --check over all six dashboard templates); both verified to FAIL when the bug is reintroduced.
Discovery verified against real state: 6 distinct projects from the local node alone, with terminal-mcp collapsing 4 checkouts into one canonical id.
NOT verified end-to-end in a browser: /dashboard/* is behind Cloudflare Access, so the final click-through needs the user's authenticated session.

items.title: P0.7 Project APIs for ChatGPT
items.description: Project-level status/submit_goal/events/report/pause/resume/assign as a pure composition over P0.1-P0.6 plus the backlog. Completes P0.
acceptance_criteria: ChatGPT can ask what a project is doing in one call
A goal can be submitted without starting work
Project pause/resume never undoes someone else's pause

deploys: terminal-mcp-http.service on a87682e, dirty:false, 15/15 local sessions intact
notes: NO new state: a test asserts the module has neither CREATE TABLE nor Migration(, and that exercising it leaves the queue schema and user_version untouched.
submit_goal records intent only -- a test asserts no queue task is created.
Pause/resume asymmetry live-smoked on the real store: a foreign 'operator: DO NOT RESUME' pause was skipped and reported, and only force=true overrode it.
assign-by-capability verified against the LIVE registry: [playwright,linux]->local, [windows]->dell-5530 (empty probed list, routed on platform), [windows,dotnet]->none.
Renamed match_verifier_nodes -> match_nodes_by_capability; P0.7 is the second caller proving it was never verifier-specific.

items.title: Backfill project_id on the 37 unscoped production queue tasks
items.description: P0.1 added queue_tasks.project_id as nullable and nothing backfilled it, so terminal_project_status reports 0 lanes / 0 tasks for the real terminal-mcp project while its backlog shows 26 open. P0.1 shipped backfill_project_ids(resolver, dry_run=True) for exactly this. DRY RUN on 2026-09-09: 37 candidates, 37 would resolve to git:github.com/hungtranbkit/terminal-mcp, 0 unresolved. It only ever fills rows where project_id IS NULL, so it cannot re-home a task that already has one. Needs an explicit decision to write to production.
acceptance_criteria: terminal_project_status shows real lanes and task counts for terminal-mcp
No task that already had a project_id is changed
Dry run reviewed before the write

tests: 184 passed across the production-data-reading suites after the write (test_project_dimension, test_verify_queue, test_project_service, test_project_mcp_tools, test_queue_store)
deploys: data-only change to ~/.local/state/terminal-mcp/queue.db; no code, no restart
notes: 37/37 scoped to git:github.com/hungtranbkit/terminal-mcp, 0 unresolved.
Live-safe backup taken first via sqlite3 .backup API (the sqlite3 CLI is NOT installed on this host -- a shell `.backup` silently produced an empty file, caught before relying on it).

Verified row-by-row, not from a summary: all 38 rows present, project_id changed on exactly 37, every change NULL -> value, NO other field (session/status/attempt_count/title/prompt) changed, and the pre-existing p0-4-smoke scope untouched. integrity ok.

Resolution was well-founded, not a path guess: claude-qtest-1/2/3 ran in three separate scratch CLONES (/home/dell/workspace/qtest-scratch-N) that normalise onto one canonical id via source=git_remote -- the many-checkouts-one-project case P0.1 exists for.

Honest scope note: all 37 are queue-development leftovers (21 CANCELLED, 15 COMPLETED, 1 BLOCKED). terminal_project_status now reports real history and throughput (15 completed over 30 days) but only 1 open task -- a simulated test blocker, not live work.

history.note: backfill applied to production and verified row-by-row

items.title: Purge queue-development test rows from the production queue
items.description: 37 queue tasks, 242 queue_events and 4 lanes from queue-v2 development (claude-qtest-1/2/3 + claude-qtest-shell-1) removed from the production queue.db, so terminal_project_status reflects real work rather than test history. Requested explicitly after the project_id backfill made them visible.
acceptance_criteria: No claude-qtest rows remain in tasks, events or lanes
No non-qtest row is altered
No orphan events reference a deleted task

tests: 201-243 passed across the production-data-reading suites after each pass
deploys: data-only change to ~/.local/state/terminal-mcp/queue.db; no code, no restart
notes: Backup queue-PREPURGE-20260909-224636.db taken first (167936 bytes, integrity ok, 38 tasks / 247 events / 37 lanes).
clear_tasks() only CANCELS, so a hard purge needed raw SQL -- done in ONE BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction across events, tasks and lanes.
Deleted: 37 tasks, 242 events, 4 lanes. Verified: every kept task row byte-identical, 0 orphan events referencing a deleted task, integrity ok, 33 lanes retained.
Also removed claude-qtest-shell-1 (1 event, 1 lane, 0 tasks) -- same test family; leaving one orphan qtest lane would have defeated the cleanup.

Second pass (same session, explicitly requested): p0-4-lease-smoke also purged -- 1 task, 5 events, 1 lane. The production queue now holds 0 tasks and 0 events; 32 lane rows remain, all empty. Schema and user_version=7 intact, integrity ok.

Third pass: 10 empty test/scratch LANE rows removed (codex-mcp-smoke-*, codex-cli-policy-*, codex-mcp-policy-*, claude-cli-policy-*, claude-mcp-policy-*, codex-policy-smoke-*). Classified against the live fleet first -- every lane belonging to a live local tmux session or a live remote session was KEPT. 22 lanes remain. DELIBERATELY NOT DELETED: window/window2 (named as protected production sessions in this codebase's own safety notes) and win4 (cannot be verified while dell-5530 is unreachable). Queue totals now: 0 tasks, 0 events, 22 lanes.

history.note: p0-4-lease-smoke purged as well; queue fully clear of test rows
10 empty test lanes purged; 3 ambiguous lanes deliberately kept
